mainTopic: Whether roofs and upper stories of ירושלים and the מקדש carry קדושה, and a new משנה on two groups eating the פסח in one room (following רבי יהודה).
overview: The גמרא asks whether roofs and upper stories share the קדושה of the place below them. It tests several sources. Saying הלל on the roofs of ירושלים proves nothing, since people may have eaten below and gone up only after the meal. The stricter upper story above the קדשי הקדשים is a special case, because its upper rooms were part of the plan ה׳ gave to דוד. The roofs of the לשכות count as holy only when they are level with the עזרה floor. This leads to a side discussion about tunnels: their status follows where they open. A ברייתא shows that roofs cannot be used for eating or slaughtering sacrifices. The words 'its roof is holy' are explained as referring to the two measuring rods kept there. The גמרא also explains how the thickness of the wall can count as inside: it refers to the low wall, whose top was level with the floor. A new משנה then teaches how two groups may eat one פסח in one room, and the גמרא shows it follows רבי יהודה against רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Trying to prove they ate the פסח on the roof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that people both ate the קרבן פסח and said הלל on the roofs. That would show roofs have the קדושה of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this mean that they ate on the roof and said הלל on the roof?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier teaching that 'the הלל split the roofs.' It suggests this means people were up on the roofs for the whole פסח meal, eating and saying הלל there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח may only be eaten inside ירושלים. If people ate it on the roofs, then the roofs must count as part of holy ירושלים. So the גמרא is reading more into the source than it states openly: not just singing, but eating too.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not...? A formula that introduces a suggested proof

steps.confusionAlert: The source text being discussed ('the הלל split the roofs') is not quoted here. It came right before it. 'מאי לאו' is building a proof from that earlier line.

phrases.english: What, is it not
phrases.notes: Formula for a suggested inference

phrases.english: that they eat [the Pesach] on the roof
and say [Hallel] on the roof!
phrases.notes: If true, roofs have the sanctity of ירושלים

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the earlier source (on the previous amud) about saying הלל on the roofs.
steps.raayaObject: Roofs in ירושלים have the קדושה of ירושלים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that the הלל 'split the roofs,' read as meaning people ate the פסח up there too.

steps.title: Maybe they ate below and only sang on the roof
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. Perhaps they ate the פסח on the ground and only went up to the roof to say הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. They ate on the ground and said הלל on the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by offering another way to read the source. Maybe only the singing happened on the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הלל does not need a holy place. Eating the פסח does. If only הלל was said on the roof, the source tells us nothing about whether roofs are holy.

phrases.english: No:
they eat on the ground
and say [Hallel] on the roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by reading the source differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not rule on whether roofs are holy.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source mentions only הלל on the roof, not eating. הלל can be said anywhere.

steps.title: The אפיקומן משנה seems to forbid changing places
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea of eating below and singing on the roof. רב explains the משנה of אפיקומן as a ban on moving from one group to another, which seems to require staying in one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But we learned in a משנה: 'We do not end after the פסח with אפיקומן.' And רב said this means people may not move themselves from one group to another group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from step 2. According to רב, people may not leave their spot and go elsewhere on פסח night, so how could they go up to the roof?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads 'אפיקומן' as 'take out the utensils,' meaning packing up to go eat somewhere else. That is forbidden. Going from the floor up to the roof looks like exactly that kind of forbidden move.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? Introduces a challenge
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
Here: moving on to eat elsewhere (according to רב)
Uproot themselves from one group to another

phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't we learn [in a Mishnah]:
We do not conclude after the Pesach with afikoman,
and Rav said:
that they may not uproot from group to group.
phrases.notes: So one must stay in one place

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָתְנַן אֵין מַפְטִירִין אַחַר הַפֶּסַח אֲפִיקוֹמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that people ate on the ground and went up to the roof for הלל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב forbids moving from group to group on פסח night, so changing location between eating and הלל should be forbidden.

steps.title: The ban on moving applies only while eating
steps.stepSummary: The ban on changing places applies only during the meal. After eating is finished, going up to the roof for הלל is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it is during the time of eating. There, it is not during the time of eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting רב's rule. Moving is forbidden only while people are still eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ban is about the meal itself: you may not split your eating between two places. Saying הלל on the roof happens after the meal, so the ban does not apply. This saves the rejection in step 2, and the proof from the roofs stays undone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. Introduces a resolution
Here... there. Splitting two cases apart

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from הלל on the roofs fails. People may have eaten below and gone up only for הלל after the meal. רב's ban on moving applies only during the eating.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, during the time of eating,
phrases.notes: רב's ban on moving

phrases.english: there, not during the time of eating.
phrases.notes: Saying הלל on the roof after the meal

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 and protects the rejection in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by time (during the meal vs. after it).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any change of place on פסח night is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only moving during the meal is forbidden. Going up for הלל afterward is fine.

steps.title: אבא שאול: the upper story above the קדשי הקדשים is stricter
steps.stepSummary: A new proof: אבא שאול teaches that the upper story above the קדשי הקדשים was entered even less often than the room itself. This suggests upper stories carry קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: אבא שאול says: The upper story of the קדשי הקדשים is stricter than the קדשי הקדשים itself. The כהן גדול enters the קדשי הקדשים once a year. But the upper story is entered only once in seven years. Some say twice in seven years. Some say once in a יובל. They enter it to check what repairs it needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to prove that upper stories are holy. It brings a ברייתא about the room above the קדשי הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the upper story were not holy, anyone could go up there whenever they liked. Instead, it was entered even more rarely than the קדשי הקדשים. That seems to show that an upper story takes on the holiness of what lies below it, and maybe even more.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. Introduces a new source as proof
The upper story above the Holy of Holies
Here: a seven-year cycle (שמיטה), not a week

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'בשבוע' means once in a seven-year cycle, not once a week. Otherwise the upper story would be entered more often than the קדשי הקדשים, not less.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
Abba Shaul says:
The upper story of the chamber of the Holy of Holies
is more stringent than the chamber of the Holy of Holies.
For the chamber of the Holy of Holies:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל נִכְנָס לוֹ פַּעַם אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: the High Priest enters it once a year,
phrases.notes: On יום כיפור

phrases.english: but the upper story of the chamber of the Holy of Holies:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נִכְנָסִין לָהּ אֶלָּא פַּעַם אַחַת בְּשָׁבוּעַ,
phrases.english: they do not enter it except once in seven years,
phrases.notes: שבוע = seven-year cycle

phrases.english: and some say: twice in seven years,
and some say: once in a Jubilee,
phrases.notes: Once in fifty years

phrases.english: to know what it needs.
phrases.notes: To check for needed repairs

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the roof proof failed, the גמרא brings a new source on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Upper stories carry the קדושה of the place below them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of אבא שאול about the upper story above the קדשי הקדשים.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the היכל is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects the proof. The היכל was built by a divine plan that explicitly included its upper rooms, so no general rule can be learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Can a person bring a proof from the היכל? The היכל is different, as it is written: 'Then דוד gave to שלמה his son the plan of the Entrance Hall, its houses, its treasuries, its upper rooms, its inner chambers, and the place of the ark cover.' And it is written: 'All this is in writing from the hand of ה׳, Who made me understand.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes off אבא שאול's proof. The היכל has its own special rules, so we cannot learn from it about roofs and upper stories in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists 'עליותיו' (its upper rooms) as part of the plan ה׳ gave in writing. So the holiness of the upper rooms in the היכל comes from that special divine plan, not from a general rule. This does not tell us whether ordinary upper stories in ירושלים or the עזרה are holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'stand up and sit down': can one really bring a proof from this?
The Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a case governed by a special פסוק cannot serve as a model for a general rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Neither proof works. The roof proof fails because הלל may have been said only after eating below. The היכל proof fails because the היכל is a special case based on a divine plan. The גמרא keeps trying other sources: the next step brings the ruling about the לשכות.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Can a person get up and argue from the Sanctuary?
phrases.notes: Rhetorical question meaning it is no proof

phrases.english: The Sanctuary is different, as it is written:
"Then David gave to Solomon his son
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 28:11

phrases.english: the pattern of the Entrance Hall and of its houses
and of its treasuries and of its upper rooms
phrases.notes: The upper rooms are explicitly part of the plan

phrases.english: and of its inner chambers and of the place of the ark cover,"
and it is written: "All is in writing
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 28:19

phrases.english: from the hand of the Lord, Who made me understand."
phrases.notes: The plan was given by ה׳

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף מֵהֵיכָל נֵיקוּם וְנִיתֵּיב אִינִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the היכל. It does not settle the general question about roofs and upper stories, which the following steps continue to examine.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The היכל's upper rooms got their status from a special divine plan stated in a פסוק, so they are not a model for other upper stories.

steps.title: New proof from the chambers whose roofs are holy
steps.stepSummary: A ruling about לשכות built in the holy area but opening to the unholy area says their insides are חול but their roofs are קודש. This seems to show that roofs carry קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Chambers built in the holy area that open to the unholy area have unholy insides and holy roofs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to prove that roofs can be holy. The ruling says the roofs of these chambers are קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling treats the inside of the room and its roof differently. The inside follows the door, which opens to חול. The roof is called קודש anyway, so it seems a roof can have קדושה of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof from a source)
Chambers or rooms in the Temple complex

phrases.english: Come and hear: The chambers built in the holy area
and opening to the unholy area —
phrases.notes: Their doors lead out to הר הבית, which has less קדושה.

phrases.english: their insides are unholy, and their roofs are holy!
phrases.notes: This is the proof: the roofs are called קודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proof from the היכל was rejected in step 6, so the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling about לשכות: 'their roofs are holy'

steps.title: The roofs were level with the courtyard floor
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that these chambers were under the ground, so their roofs were simply part of the courtyard floor. That is why the roofs are holy. It proves nothing about ordinary roofs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא explained it: This is when their roofs are level with the ground of the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא pushes off the proof. The chambers were dug under the עזרה, so their 'roof' is really just the courtyard floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the roof is level with the courtyard, walking on it means walking in the עזרה itself. Its קדושה comes from being courtyard ground, not from being a roof. So this case teaches nothing about raised roofs or upper stories.

keyTerms.meaning: He interpreted it (explained the source in a limited way)
The ground of the Temple courtyard

phrases.english: Rav Chisda interpreted it:
when their roofs are level with the ground of the courtyard.
phrases.notes: The rooms are underground, and their tops form part of the עזרה floor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 7 by narrowing the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ruling about לשכות only covers roofs that are level with the courtyard floor.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed these were ordinary raised roofs. In fact the roofs were part of the courtyard ground itself.

steps.title: The second half of the ruling would make tunnels holy
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the same ruling says chambers built in the unholy area but opening to the holy area have holy insides. Under רב חסדא's reading those rooms would be underground tunnels, and רבי יוחנן said tunnels are not holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the second half: chambers built in the unholy area that open to the holy area have holy insides and unholy roofs. If you think their roofs are level with the courtyard floor, they are tunnels, and רבי יוחנן said tunnels were not sanctified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's explanation. It uses the second half of the same ruling to show that his reading leads to a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every case in this ruling has rooms under the ground, then the rooms in the second half are also underground, which makes them tunnels. Yet the ruling says their insides are קודש. That directly contradicts רבי יוחנן, who said tunnels never received קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your explanation is right)
Say the latter part of the source
It enters your mind (if you were to think)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the rooms are built under the unholy area, yet their insides are holy because they open to the holy area. In this ruling, where the door opens decides the status of the inside.

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
if they were built in the unholy area and open to the holy area —
their insides are holy and their roofs are unholy.
And if it enters your mind
that this is when their roofs are level with the courtyard ground,
then they are tunnels,
phrases.notes: Underground rooms count as tunnels.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan said:
tunnels were not sanctified!
phrases.notes: Yet the ruling calls their insides holy, so there is a contradiction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's explanation from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's reading that the roofs were level with the courtyard ground
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applied to the second half of the ruling, his reading turns the rooms into tunnels with holy insides. That contradicts רבי יוחנן's rule that tunnels are not holy.

steps.title: It depends on where the tunnel opens
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן was talking about tunnels that open to הר הבית. The ruling about לשכות is talking about rooms that open to the עזרה. Those do become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן said this, he meant tunnels that open to הר הבית. When that source was taught, it meant rooms that open to the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two sources are talking about different tunnels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tunnels are not holy in general. But a tunnel whose door opens into the עזרה takes on the courtyard's קדושה. So רבי יוחנן and the ruling about לשכות do not argue, and רב חסדא's reading still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: When he said (introduces a limiting of a statement)
The Temple Mount, which has lower קדושה than the courtyard

phrases.english: When Rabbi Yochanan said it —
it was about tunnels opening to the Temple Mount.
When that source was taught —
it was about rooms opening to the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two sources describe different tunnels
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's rule seemed to cover all tunnels.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only tunnels opening to הר הבית are not holy. Tunnels opening to the עזרה are holy.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even tunnels under the היכל are unholy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying that tunnels under the היכל itself are חול. This seems to show that tunnels are never holy, even under the holiest building.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: רבי יהודה says, the tunnels under the היכל are unholy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 10 with a ברייתא of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tunnels under the היכל would surely lead into the holy area, yet רבי יהודה calls them חול. That seems to show that tunnels never get קדושה, whatever they open to.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The tunnels beneath the Sanctuary are unholy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that tunnels opening to the holy area are holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even tunnels directly under the היכל are called חול, so tunnels seem to be unholy no matter where they open.

steps.title: Those tunnels opened to the unholy area
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's tunnels under the היכל opened outward to the unholy area, so they were חול. This matches the rule that the door decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that was taught, it meant tunnels that open to the unholy area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה was talking about tunnels whose doors led out to חול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even under the היכל, a tunnel that opens to חול stays חול. This confirms the rule from step 10: where the door opens decides the status of the inside.
steps.whatToRemember: For tunnels and underground rooms, the status of the inside follows where the door opens: open to the holy area means holy, open to the unholy area means חול.

phrases.english: When that was taught —
it was about tunnels that open to the unholy area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): this ברייתא is about tunnels opening to חול
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to say that all tunnels under the היכל are חול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only tunnels opening to חול are unholy, even when they lie under the היכל.

steps.title: New proof: the roof of the היכל is holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier source about the היכל, which also says 'its roof is holy.' The roof is not mentioned in the divine plan, so רב יוסף's rejection does not cover it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: And its roof is holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier היכל source to try a new proof that roofs are holy. This step sets up the answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said in step 6 that the upper rooms were holy only because the divine plan included them. The roof of the היכל is not part of that plan, yet the source still calls it holy. So it seems roofs are holy in general.

keyTerms.meaning: Its roof (the roof of the היכל)

phrases.english: Come and hear: And its roof is holy!
phrases.notes: A line from a source about the היכל saying its roof is holy. The roof is not listed in the plan in רב יוסף's פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proof from the לשכות is finished, so the גמרא goes back to the היכל source from steps 5–6 with a new angle.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The source about the היכל: 'and its roof is holy.' The roof is not in the divine plan, so רב יוסף's rejection does not apply.

steps.title: A teaching says these roofs are not holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from 'its roof is holy' by quoting a ברייתא that says sacrifices may not be eaten or slaughtered on these roofs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think that? It is taught: on these roofs you may not eat קדשי קדשים, and you may not slaughter קדשים קלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the proof from Step 13. It quotes a ברייתא showing that roofs do not have the holiness of the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 tried to prove something from the words 'its roof is holy.' This ברייתא says plainly that on the roofs you cannot do the two main things that need עזרה holiness: eating קדשי קדשים and slaughtering קדשים קלים. So the roof cannot be holy in the way the proof needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And can you really think so?!' A strong rejection of what was just said
The holiest sacrifices, which may only be eaten inside the עזרה
Sacrifices of lesser holiness, which must be slaughtered inside the עזרה

phrases.english: And can you understand it that way?!
But it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: גַּגִּין הַלָּלוּ אֵין אוֹכְלִין שָׁם קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: On these roofs one may not eat offerings of the most sacred order there,
and one may not slaughter offerings of lesser sanctity there!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the roof has עזרה holiness
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא says explicitly that the roofs lack the holiness needed for eating or slaughtering sacrifices

steps.title: Then what does 'its roof is holy' mean?
steps.stepSummary: If roofs are not holy, the earlier source that said 'its roof is holy' now becomes hard to understand.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, it is difficult: the source said 'its roof is holy'!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that roofs are shown to be not holy, the גמרא asks about the earlier source that said the היכל's roof is holy. How can both be true?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources now clash. The ברייתא says roofs are not holy, but the source about the היכל says 'its roof is holy.' The גמרא needs an explanation of what kind of holiness the roof had.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But then it is difficult.' The problem now shifts to a different source
'Its roof is holy.' The phrase from the source about the היכל

phrases.english: But then it is difficult: its roof is sanctified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from Step 14 to raise a problem with the source quoted in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The source that says the היכל's roof is holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says roofs are not holy for sacrifices, so the statement 'its roof is holy' seems to contradict it

steps.title: The roof was holy because of the two measuring rods
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר גוריא explains that 'its roof is holy' is about the two measuring rods (אמות) kept there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר גוריא said: it refers to those two measuring cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא בר גוריא answers the problem. The roof is called holy only in connection with the two measuring rods, not as a place for sacrifices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roof did not have the holiness of the עזרה for eating or slaughtering. It was 'holy' in a narrower sense, because of the special measuring rods that belonged there. So the ברייתא and the source about the היכל do not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives this answer
Cubits. Here it means measuring rods one cubit long

phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said:
It refers to those two cubits (measuring rods).
phrases.notes: The roof is called holy only because of these measuring rods

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the meaning of the source: the 'holiness' is for a narrow purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Its roof is holy' means the roof has full עזרה holiness
steps.terutzMaskana: The roof is holy only because of the two measuring rods kept there, not for sacrifices

steps.title: The משנה about the two measuring rods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה describing two cubit rods in שושן הבירה, each a bit longer than the standard cubit of משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: there were two cubit rods in שושן הבירה. One was on the northeast corner and one on the southeast corner. The northeast one was half a finger longer than the cubit of משה. The southeast one was half a finger longer than that. So it was a full finger longer than the cubit of משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show where these 'two cubits' come from. It describes the two rods and their exact lengths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were three lengths: the standard cubit of משה, a rod half a finger longer, and a rod a full finger longer. The two longer rods are the 'two cubits' רב חמא בר גוריא was talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As we learned in a משנה.' Introduces a supporting source
'Shushan the capital.' A place in the מקדש named after the Persian capital
The standard cubit from the time of משה
A finger-width, a small unit of measure

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
There were two cubit rods in Shushan the Capital,
one on the northeast corner
and one on the southeast corner.
The one on the northeast corner

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה יְתֵירָה עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה חֲצִי אֶצְבַּע,
phrases.english: was longer than that of Moses by half a fingerbreadth,
and the one on the southeast corner
was longer than it by half a fingerbreadth,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצֵאת יְתֵירָה עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה אֶצְבַּע.
phrases.english: so it turns out to be longer than that of Moses by a fingerbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the 'two cubits' mentioned in Step 16
steps.raayaObject: The existence of the two special cubit rods
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (in מסכת כלים) about the two cubits in שושן הבירה

steps.title: Why were there a larger and a smaller cubit?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks why the builders had one large cubit and one small cubit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was there one large cubit and one small cubit?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a question to set up its next line. Why have measuring sticks of different sizes at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems odd to keep cubits of different lengths in the מקדש. The answer will explain a practical reason connected to paying workers.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָמָה הָיוּ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה?
phrases.english: And why was there one large and one small?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָה הָיוּ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the different lengths described in Step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of having cubits of different sizes

steps.title: So the workers would not misuse holy money
steps.stepSummary: Workers were paid by the small cubit but delivered work by the large cubit, so they would never take more than they earned.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that the craftsmen would take payment by the small cubit and give back work by the large cubit, so they would not come to מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question. The different sizes protect the workers from taking מקדש money they did not earn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money of the מקדש is הקדש, and using it improperly is מעילה. If a worker was paid even a tiny bit too much, he would be guilty of מעילה. By measuring their pay with a shorter cubit and their work with a longer one, they always gave a little extra, so they were safe.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how careful the מקדש was to protect people from accidentally misusing holy funds.

phrases.english: So that the craftsmen would take by the small one
and return by the large one,
so that they would not come to misuse consecrated property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Paying by the small cubit and receiving work by the large one keeps workers from taking unearned הקדש money

steps.title: Why were two larger cubits needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why there needed to be two extra-long cubits instead of just one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question, setting up the next answer. One longer cubit would seem to be enough to prevent מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The standard cubit of משה could serve as the 'small' one. So why add two longer rods, one half a finger longer and one a full finger longer?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need two?' Asks why there is more than one

steps.confusionAlert: Both rods in שושן הבירה are longer than the cubit of משה. The question is not about the standard cubit, but about why there were two longer ones.

phrases.english: And why do I need two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer of Step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why two longer cubit rods were needed

steps.title: One for gold and silver, one for building
steps.stepSummary: One longer cubit was used for silver and gold work, and the other for construction.
steps.simpleTranslation: One was for silver and gold, and one was for building.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each longer cubit had its own job. One was for precious-metal work and one was for building work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For silver and gold work they used the rod that was only half a finger longer. With costly materials, a full extra finger would make the workers lose too much. For building work they used the rod a full finger longer.
steps.whatToRemember: The roof of the היכל was not holy for sacrifices. It was called 'holy' only because of the two measuring rods: workers were paid by a smaller cubit and gave work by a larger one, to avoid מעילה.

phrases.english: One was for silver and gold,
and one was for construction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two longer rods had different uses: precious metals and construction

steps.title: Our משנה: windows and wall thickness count as inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to our משנה, which says the windows and the thickness of the wall count as inside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: the windows and the thickness of the wall are like inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line in our משנה to start a new discussion. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says the window spaces and the thick wall of the עזרה have the same holiness as the inside. The גמרא is about to ask how that can work, since we just saw that raised places like roofs are not holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Like inside, having the holiness of the inside

phrases.english: We learned in the mishna:
The windows and the thickness of the wall are considered like inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the conclusion just reached (raised places like roofs lack עזרה holiness) to a line of our משנה, setting up the question in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The windows and the thickness of the עזרה wall have the holiness of the inside

steps.title: How can the thick wall be level with the floor?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that windows can be level with the courtyard floor, but asks how the wall's thickness ever could be.
steps.simpleTranslation: The windows are fine: you can find them level with the floor of the עזרה. But the thickness of the wall, how can you find that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the line of the משנה about the wall. It accepts the windows but asks how the wall's thickness can be holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A window opening can sit at floor level, so it makes sense that it counts as inside. But the top of a wall is high above the floor. Since even roofs are not holy, how can the wall's thickness count as inside?

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is fine.' Accepts one part before challenging another part
'You can find it,' meaning there is a real case

phrases.english: Granted, the windows,
you can find it when it is level with the floor of the courtyard.
But the thickness of the wall,
how can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling quoted in Step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the thickness of the wall is like inside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only places level with the floor of the עזרה are holy (raised places like roofs are not). Windows can be level with the floor, but the wall's thickness seems to always be raised

steps.title: The low outer wall solves the problem
steps.stepSummary: The thickness of a wall can be level with the courtyard floor in the case of the low wall (בר שורא), which the verse in איכה hints at.
steps.simpleTranslation: You find it with the low wall. As it says: 'He made the rampart and the wall mourn.' And רבי אחא said (some say רבי חנינא): this means a wall and a low wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 23. There was a low wall whose top was level with the floor of the עזרה, so its thickness could count as part of the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 asked how a wall's thickness could ever be level with the עזרה floor. The answer points to a special low wall standing next to the main wall. The proof is that the verse uses two words, חֵל and חוֹמָה, which teaches there were two walls: a regular one and a low one.

keyTerms.meaning: A low wall; literally 'son of a wall'
You can find it (a case where this works)
A rampart or low outer wall

steps.whatToRemember: The wall-thickness case in the משנה refers to the low wall (בר שורא), whose top was level with the עזרה floor.

phrases.english: You find it in the case of the low wall,
as it is written: 'He made the rampart and wall mourn,'
phrases.notes: איכה 2:8

phrases.english: and Rabbi Acha said,
and some say it was Rabbi Chanina:
a wall and a low wall.
phrases.notes: The double wording points to two separate walls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a specific case where the problem disappears
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No wall's thickness could ever be level with the courtyard floor.
steps.terutzMaskana: The low wall's top was level with the עזרה floor, so its thickness counts as inside the courtyard.

steps.title: Two groups eating in one room
steps.stepSummary: Two groups sharing one house for the פסח each face their own direction and eat, with the hot-water pot in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Two groups eating in one house. These turn their faces one way and eat, and those turn their faces the other way and eat, and the hot-water pot is in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It allows two separate groups to eat the פסח in the same room, as long as each group faces its own way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group must eat as its own separate unit, so facing away keeps the groups visibly separate. Sharing one hot-water pot in the middle is still allowed, so a single waiter can easily serve both groups.

keyTerms.meaning: A registered group eating the קרבן פסח together

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying the groups merge into one. They stay two separate groups, even though they share a room and a pot.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Two groups that were eating
in one house,

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ הוֹפְכִין אֶת פְּנֵיהֶם הֵילָךְ וְאוֹכְלִין,
phrases.english: these turn their faces this way and eat,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הוֹפְכִין אֶת פְּנֵיהֶם הֵילָךְ וְאוֹכְלִין,
phrases.english: and those turn their faces that way and eat,
and the hot-water pot is in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁתֵּי חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלִין בְּבַיִת אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two groups may eat in one house if each faces its own direction. A shared hot-water pot between them is allowed.

steps.title: The waiter and the bride
steps.stepSummary: The waiter serving the other group closes his mouth and turns away until he returns to his own group. A bride may turn her face away from her group and eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the waiter gets up to pour, he closes his mouth and turns his face until he reaches his own group, and then he eats. And the bride turns her face and eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with two special cases. It tells us how a waiter serving both groups must behave, and that a shy bride may face away from her group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While serving the other group, the waiter must not look like he is eating with them, so he keeps his mouth shut and his face turned. The bride is an exception: out of modesty she may turn away from her own group, even though this might make her look like part of the other group.

keyTerms.meaning: To pour or mix a drink

phrases.english: When the waiter gets up to pour,

phrases.aramaic: קוֹפֵץ אֶת פִּיו וּמַחֲזִיר אֶת פָּנָיו,
phrases.english: he closes his mouth and turns his face,
until he reaches his own group and eats.
And the bride turns her face and eats.
phrases.notes: Out of modesty in front of men she doesn't know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the special cases of the waiter and the bride.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waiter must not eat while serving the other group. A bride may turn away from her group and eat.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא our משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking which תנא wrote this משנה. This sets up the next move: it will name the תנא and then bring a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes that one פסח can be eaten by two groups in one house. Not every תנא agrees with that, so the גמרא wants to know who holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: Our mishnah, whose view is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the new משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that one פסח may be eaten by two groups in one house.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי יהודה as the author of the משנה. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a short answer. The ברייתא that follows will show that רבי יהודה allows one פסח to be split between groups.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view the משנה follows

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 27.

steps.title: Verses: two groups allowed, but each eater stays in one place
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'the houses' that one פסח may be eaten by two groups. It learns from 'in one house it shall be eaten' that a single eater may not eat in two places.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'Upon the houses in which they will eat it' teaches that the פסח may be eaten in two groups. I might think one eater may eat in two places, so the verse says: 'In one house it shall be eaten.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יהודה allows splitting one פסח between groups. The same ברייתא also sets a limit: one person may not eat it in two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word 'houses' shows that one animal can be shared by more than one group. The singular 'one house' is then read as a rule about each eater, who must finish eating in one spot. This is the basis for the משנה's two groups in one room.

keyTerms.meaning: In one house it shall be eaten

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
'Upon the houses in which they shall eat it,'
phrases.notes: שמות 12:7

phrases.english: this teaches that the Paschal lamb may be eaten in two groups.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יְהֵא הָאוֹכֵל אוֹכֵל בִּשְׁתֵּי מְקוֹמוֹת —
phrases.english: I might think the one who eats may eat in two places —
therefore the verse says: 'In one house it shall be eaten.'
phrases.notes: שמות 12:46

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 28 that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה (two groups in one house) follows רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the verses 'the houses' and 'in one house it shall be eaten'

steps.title: The waiter who ate by the oven
steps.stepSummary: A waiter who ate a כזית by the oven should eat his fill there, since he cannot eat it anywhere else. The group may come sit next to him as a favor. The ברייתא is labeled as רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: a waiter who ate a כזית next to the oven, if he is smart, fills his stomach from it. And if the group wants to do him a favor, they come and sit beside him. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the 'eat in one place' rule to a practical case and ends by naming רבי יהודה. That name confirms the גמרא's claim that our משנה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By eating a כזית at the oven, the waiter has fixed that spot as his eating place. He cannot continue at the table later, so the smart move is to eat all he wants right away. The group can let him keep eating by moving to sit with him. The closing words 'דברי רבי יהודה' prove the ברייתא, and so the משנה, is רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's volume, the minimum amount for eating

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, one פסח may be split among groups, but each person must finish eating in the one place where he started. That is why the משנה is attributed to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'each eater stays in one place' explains the משנה's careful instructions for the waiter. He must not eat while serving the other group.

phrases.english: From here they said:
a waiter who ate an olive-bulk next to the oven,

phrases.aramaic: אִי פִּקֵּחַ הוּא מְמַלֵּא כְּרֵיסוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ,
phrases.english: if he is smart, he fills his stomach from it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם רָצוּ בְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה לַעֲשׂוֹת עִמּוֹ טוֹבָה —
phrases.english: and if the members of the group want to do him a favor —
they come and sit beside him,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, applying its rule and naming רבי יהודה as its author.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the waiter eats a כזית by the oven, that spot is his only eating place. He should eat his fill there, or the group may join him there.

steps.title: רבי שמעון allows one person to eat the פסח in two places
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from the plural word 'the houses' that one eater may eat the פסח in two different places.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'Upon the houses in which they shall eat it' teaches that one person who eats may eat in two places.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and brings רבי שמעון, who disagrees with רבי יהודה. He says one person may eat the פסח in two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used 'the houses' (plural) to teach that two groups may share one פסח. He used 'in one house' to forbid one eater from eating in two places. רבי שמעון reads the plural 'houses' as being about the individual eater, so one person may move and eat in a second place.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who argues with רבי יהודה here
The houses (plural), the word in the פסוק that רבי שמעון learns from
It teaches: a phrase used to bring a lesson from a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two תנאים. רבי יהודה says a single eater may NOT eat in two places, and our משנה follows him. רבי שמעון says a single eater MAY.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why the גמרא tied our משנה to רבי יהודה. Under רבי שמעון, the waiter would not need to stay by the oven.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
"Upon the houses
in which they shall eat it"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:7

phrases.english: teaches that the one who eats may eat
in two places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing תנא's view inside the same ברייתא that was attributed to רבי יהודה in steps 29-30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, a single person may eat the קרבן פסח in two places, based on the plural 'houses.'
